newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Music industry calls on Irish govt to protect jobs.
newsitem.headline: Music industry calls on Irish govt to protect jobs.

text.p: Music industry representatives on Wednesday called on the Irish government to use its tenure as EU president to push for increased copyright protection for the $24 billion European music industry.

Irish and international record industry bodies, IRMA and IFPI, warned government officials at a Dublin meeting that with strong growth in on-line services such as the Internet, Irish jobs were at stake in the current EU review of copyright rules.
The meeting comes on the eve of a joint EU-Irish conference in Clare, west Ireland, to discuss ways of promoting the music industry in Europe.
The music bodies urged Ireland to back a pan EU campaign for reduced value added tax (VAT) on recorded music and a crack down on piracy, which they said cost the industry $2.1 billion each year.

"Copyright-based industries account for 6.0 percent of the (EU) community's GDP, and the music industry is a leading force in that sector and is a significant earner of foreign revenue," IRMA chairman Paul Keogh said in a statement.
Keogh said a failure to regulate the on-line market would result in widespread piracy and a significant portion of these revenues would flow out of the EU.
IFPI director general Nicholas Garnett said Europe's recording industry is one of the key growth industries of the future and a vast investor in local culture.

"EU and national policies should reflect that - not with handouts and subsidies, but with tough action to promote investment, open markets, end discrimination with other cultural goods and stamp out piracy," Garnett said.
